title: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors
description: Promote worksite or product safety by applying knowledge of industrial processes, mechanics, chemistry, psychology, and industrial health and safety laws. Includes industrial product safety engineers.

tasks.text: Investigate industrial accidents, injuries, or occupational diseases to determine causes and preventive measures.
Conduct research to evaluate safety levels for products.
Evaluate product designs for safety.
Evaluate potential health hazards or damage that could occur from product misuse.
Evaluate adequacy of actions taken to correct health inspection violations.
Interview employers and employees to obtain information about work environments and workplace incidents.
Review employee safety programs to determine their adequacy.
Plan and conduct industrial hygiene research.
Compile, analyze, and interpret statistical data related to occupational illnesses and accidents.
Report or review findings from accident investigations, facilities inspections, or environmental testing.
Participate in preparation of product usage and precautionary label instructions.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Recommend procedures for detection, prevention, and elimination of physical, chemical, or other product hazards.
Provide technical advice and guidance to organizations on how to handle health-related problems and make needed changes.
Develop industry standards of product safety.
Write and revise safety regulations and codes.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Maintain liaisons with outside organizations, such as fire departments, mutual aid societies, and rescue teams, so that emergency responses can be facilitated.
Confer with medical professionals to assess health risks and to develop ways to manage health issues and concerns.
Conduct or direct testing of air quality, noise, temperature, or radiation levels to verify compliance with health and safety regulations.
Check floors of plants to ensure that they are strong enough to support heavy machinery.
Design and build safety equipment.
Install safety devices on machinery or direct device installation.
Conduct or coordinate worker training in areas such as safety laws and regulations, hazardous condition monitoring, and use of safety equipment.
Maintain and apply knowledge of current policies, regulations, and industrial processes.
Interpret safety regulations for others interested in industrial safety, such as safety engineers, labor representatives, and safety inspectors.
Review plans and specifications for construction of new machinery or equipment to determine whether all safety requirements have been met.
Provide expert testimony in litigation cases.
Inspect facilities, machinery, or safety equipment to identify and correct potential hazards, and to ensure safety regulation compliance.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Electronic design automation EDA software, Mathsoft Mathcad, Roof support design software.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Microsoft SharePoint, Records management software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
